headline: Texas ICE agent indicted for striking fleeing Houston pedestrian with vehicle
summary: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has been indicted by a Harris County grand jury for aggravated assault, following an incident where he allegedly drove his vehicle into a man, Miguel Parra-Hernandez. The indictment suggests potential misconduct by an ICE agent, which could impact public trust in immigration enforcement agencies.

headline: Bird flu spreads to Washington dairy farms
summary: In Washington state, bird flu is rapidly spreading among dairy farms, with 27 confirmed cases in just three weeks. Although the risk to humans is low, public health officials advise consuming only pasteurized milk. The virus is challenging to contain due to its unknown transmission methods. State veterinarians are conducting weekly tests in affected areas. Symptoms in cattle include decreased milk production and respiratory issues.

headline: California can’t afford to keep Prop 13 loopholes open when billions of dollars are on the line
summary: California faces budget pressures due to federal cuts in healthcare and food aid, potentially leading to a $20 billion annual deficit. Closing Prop 13's commercial and industrial loopholes could generate up to $25.1 billion annually for state and local governments, easing budget strain. The incoming governor and legislature have an opportunity to use this revenue to fund programs that protect families and increase trust in government, such as transitional kindergarten expansion, while addressing the state's fiscal challenges.

headline: For the record: Fresno man deported by ICE had previous illegal crossings
summary: ICE criticized California news outlet CalMatters for not disclosing a deported immigrant's criminal history and repeated deportations, but did not respond to reporter's requests for comment before publication.

headline: Did Trump invest more money in rural California health ahead of the election?
summary: California received notice of a $233.6 million award for rural healthcare improvements, part of a national $50 billion federal investment. The funding aims to bolster rural hospitals, some of which have closed or struggled due to financial challenges. The federal legislation includes Medicaid cuts, which could potentially leave 2 million Californians without health coverage, doubling the state's uninsured rate. This impacts Public Health by potentially increasing disease outbreaks and healthcare disparities in rural areas.

headline: Shakopee man from Nicaragua deported to Central African Republic
summary: Kenis Lopez Gonzalez, a Nicaraguan immigrant with a U.S. court order blocking his deportation due to torture risks, was deported to the unstable Central African Republic by ICE during Operation Metro Surge. This raises concerns about U.S. immigration enforcement's compliance with protective orders and potential human rights violations in third-country deportations.

headline: Secretary of education says Virginia will ‘move the achievement needle forward’
summary: Gov. Spanberger's administration is prioritizing early education and college readiness for K-12 students, aiming to close childcare affordability gaps and expand career tech education. The Board of Education discussed Smith's plans, which focus on improving teaching quality, literacy instruction, and student well-being. Lawmakers will discuss education legislation starting Jan. 13.

headline: Louisiana health officials warn against amoeba infections from tap water
summary: The Louisiana Department of Health has warned the public against using tap water for nasal rinses and contact lens storage due to two serious Acanthamoeba infections this year, including one fatal case. Although tap water hasn't been confirmed as the source, the department advises using distilled or boiled water in neti pots and for contact lens care to prevent rare but potentially fatal infections.

headline: Huge bipartisan majorities of Ohioans want a fix to Social Security, new poll shows
summary: Ohioans overwhelmingly (85%) want Social Security fixed to prevent a 22% benefit cut in 2032, with Republicans, Democrats, and independents united on this issue. Awareness of the pending insolvency is low, but voters prioritize candidates with plans to prevent automatic cuts. Both major U.S. Senate candidates in Ohio express concern but lack detailed plans to address Social Security's funding crisis.

headline: Hayes takes over Finance as Ferguson announces early changes to leadership
summary: Senator Antonio Hayes will chair the Senate Finance Committee, the first Black lawmaker to do so. Cory McCray, also Black, will serve as vice-chair of the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, which faces a $3 billion structural budget gap. The budget may see cuts and tax increases, including possible changes to the state's 6% sales tax.

headline: Howard lawmakers’ bill would set higher tax rates on propose ICE facility in Elkridge
summary: Howard County lawmakers introduced a bill allowing them to set higher property and transfer taxes on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility in Elkridge, aiming to compensate for fiscal impacts on the county. The bill comes after a federal court rejected the county's emergency legislation blocking the facility's permit. Community members support the bill, viewing it as a response to federal immigration policies. ICE stated no tax would stop deportations.

headline: Trump and Freedom Caucus approval, election confidence: Three takeaways from a Wyoming survey ahead of the general election
summary: Wyoming Survey & Analysis Center's 2026 poll: More disapprove than approve of Trump's job performance; majority disapproves of Wyoming Freedom Caucus, but it's close; most Wyomingites confident in state elections.

headline: During wave of closures, Morrisey says school funding issue will ‘dominate’ 2027 legislative session
summary: Governor Morrisey prioritizes addressing school funding issues in the upcoming legislative session, with eight to 20 schools facing closure or consolidation due to inadequate funding. The state school board proposes restructuring the school funding formula to address declining enrollment and special education needs, but previous multi-million dollar proposals faced resistance from lawmakers. Morrisey cautions against simply increasing spending, instead focusing on efficient use of funds. The session begins in January.
